about: Lesson A14 (a14-microgrid-value), 2026-11-03. One price year: 2025 dollars. Real: the outage costs of a 2025 survey of rural electric cooperative members (Berkeley Lab and partners, ICE Calculator 2 initiative, report dated November 2026: Tables 4-2, 4-4, 5-2 and 5-4, the point estimates; the executive summary's Tables ES-2 and ES-3 print the upper confidence bounds for non-residential members, so the body tables are used), EIA's 2025 average retail prices (Electric Power Monthly, Table 5.3) and FERC's 2024 Energy Primer (pp. 35, 36 and 130). Illustrative: Prairie Campus, its hospital's cost per hour, the outage pattern, every equipment cost, the borrowing rates and the village; they are round numbers in 2025 dollars, not quotes. The village's households, mill and sun are lesson F7's (assets/learn/data/f07-microgrids.json); the test checks they agree. Research text: the Real-world box quotes approved excerpts E8.4, E8.6 and E8.7 (reports/learn/excerpts_for_approval.md) on the page.

owners.label: The utility
owners.pays: All the utility's customers, through rates its state regulator approves
owners.gains: The hospital (backup); all customers (the everyday savings lower the utility's costs)
owners.risk: The customers, if the regulator lets the cost into rates; the utility's shareholders, if not

owners.label: A rural co-op
owners.pays: The co-op's members, through their rates
owners.gains: The hospital, a member (backup); all members (everyday savings)
owners.risk: The members: the co-op borrows, and has no shares to sell

owners.label: The county
owners.gains: The county hospital (backup); the county (everyday savings)

owners.label: A private company
owners.pays: The campus: a fixed yearly fee in a long contract
owners.gains: The campus (backup and everyday savings, less the fee); the company (its return)
owners.risk: The company carries cost overruns and breakdowns; the campus pays the fee even in calm years

facts.what: What an 8-hour outage costs, on average, a household and a business on a rural co-op (2025 survey).
facts.source: Berkeley Lab and partners, ICE Calculator 2 co-op report, Tables 4-2 and 5-2

facts.what: A household's loss per kWh not delivered in an 8-hour outage, against the average U.S. residential price of a kWh in 2025.
facts.source: Berkeley Lab report, Table 4-4; EIA, Electric Power Monthly, Table 5.3

facts.what: Electric cooperatives and municipal utilities in the United States.
Share of the surveyed co-ops' business members with backup generation on site.
